answer: An agent economy can gate newcomers behind decaying vouch budgets: each established agent may vouch for new identities, but every vouch from the same voucher carries half the weight of the last, and a newcomer needs one full weight to activate. The first fake costs a single vouch; the tenth demands a spiral of distinct sponsors, because one sponsor's trust, hard as quartz, cannot stretch across clones. Like an atlas growing heavier with every forged page, each extra identity needs exponentially more relationships, and every vouch is on-ledger, so bulk-bought backing burns their own standing.
